about: The declared coral pairs' tell-apart lines for the quiz feedback's one decisive line (Pierre, 2026-11-18, the feedback sheet study's question (d); docs/decisions/2026-11-18-tellapart-lines.md): every pair of data.json gen and x.gen genera that one of them declares in its look, the slate's and those with a bonus or Key-only genus (docs/decisions/2026-11-20-tellapart-bonus-pairs.md). Our own words, short and plain, each side describing its own genus with its sources: the IMR lecture first (the genus's notes and slides as data.json imr and sl hold them), then the Coral Finder (the genus's criteria as data.json crit holds them, on its pages), then Corals of the World for genera with no IMR notes. A side is written only when its sources say it of that genus, and a pair only when the two sides really tell the genera apart; none lists the pairs left with the first ID tip, and why. tools/apply_coral_apart.py checks them and writes data.json ap and apsrc; quiz.js fbLine shows them.

none.Acropora|Cyphastrea: the sources disagree: Corals of the World gives Cyphastrea decadia, the one Cyphastrea confirmed in the Philippines (iNaturalist Research Grade there and the Corals of the World checklist, 2026-11-19), Acropora-like axial corallites, while the Coral Finder says Cyphastrea's tip corallite is undifferentiated; a discrepancy for Pierre (rule C5), not a line
none.Anacropora|Montipora: both have small, empty-looking corallites; IMR and the Coral Finder give Anacropora a smooth surface but say Montipora's surface varies, so bumps are no sure difference, and no source read compares the two (Corals of the World's Anacropora forbesi page names only other Anacropora as similar, read 2026-11-19)
none.Astreopora|Turbinaria: the sources describe different things on each side (Astreopora's corallites lined with spinules, Turbinaria's smooth surface between the corallites), so the contrast would be implied, not read; no source compares the two (Corals of the World's Astreopora myriophthalma page names only other Astreopora as similar, read 2026-11-19)
none.Cycloseris|Lithophyllon: both have fine septal teeth (the Coral Finder, p. 64 and 67), so the one difference read is size and soft sediment, while the Cycloseris page says it is easily taken for a young Lithophyllon; no source read gives a feature of Lithophyllon beside Cycloseris's (Corals of the World's Cycloseris cyclolites page names only another Cycloseris as similar, read 2026-11-20)
none.Duncanopsammia|Goniopora: both show large polyps by day; the only difference read is the colony's form (plates against massive or columns), and no source gives Duncanopsammia's tentacles beside Goniopora's 24 (Corals of the World's Turbinaria peltata page, now D. peltata, compares it only with Turbinaria, read 2026-11-19)
